title: Documentation overhaul and reusable Papyrus wiki/help
description:
Design-only planning requested by Ryan during voice. Implementation remains unstarted; no code, infrastructure, deployment, purchase or publishing authorization is implied. Initial status stays open (Discovery), unassigned.

As a Papyrus user, editor and application integrator, I want trustworthy workflow documentation and a reusable structured Markus wiki/help experience, so that products can explain their behavior without each building a bespoke documentation system.

Planning only. Preserve existing M10 PPY-2156fa static-publishing/README deliverables and wiki-lifecycle epic PPY-964472; this broader overhaul coordinates current and planned workflows rather than repeating their implementation. Workflow-owned documentation behavior stories belong under Monitoring, Editorial triage, RSS and headless milestones; cross-cutting review tasks here verify those links, current truth and discoverability.

Product direction: Papyrus authors/edits structured Markus docs; conventional Help entry opens the appropriate wiki/help. Consumers use a shared exported UI dependency with per-app theming. An optional configurable RAG chat sidebar retrieves only within the correct publication/knowledge base and existing access permissions, and answers cite sources. No repository creation, implementation, migration, deployment, indexing, model calls or purchase is authorized. A new repository was only a tentative idea; package/repository boundaries remain open.

Grounded inspection: private AnthusAI/Chattic.us-web main at 0f92209b02e9c292d5f59440996d1a7136810778 already has publication/build.py calling Papyrus build_markus_site and SiteChrome, publication/catalog.py for idea/product wiki pages and blog related links, styles/markus-chatticus.css, generated wiki metadata, heading anchors, canonical/OG handling and marketing_wiki.feature. Its product docs come from Chatticus docs/LICENSE rather than copies of internal Kanbus wiki material. The older local checkout at 3796bb13 contains now-obsolete WikiPageView/WikiIndex wrappers, so do not use that as the current migration baseline. No RAG sidebar was established by this scoped source inventory; do not claim one exists or must be replaced. PPY-7417c5 and PPY-917578 already track Chatticus migration and record landed slices; build source is not evidence of live deployment.

Definition of Done for future delivery: mapped and reviewed workflow guides, shared authoring/presentation contracts, conventional Help, themed dependency reuse, scoped source-citing optional chat, migration/reuse assessment, and representative cross-product dogfooding. Actual config, backend authorization and retrieval capabilities must be verified during later implementation; a separate architecture investigation owns deep backend analysis.

Approved unified page/wiki architecture, planning only: use one page/content system with paths. The homepage is an ordinary editable Markus page at `/`; product pages under `/features` and documentation under `/wiki` are ordinary content subtrees in that same system. Wiki denotes navigation and presentation, not a separate storage model, authoring backend, publication lifecycle or publishing engine. Reuse the existing content lifecycle, publishing projection and reader-access rules; avoid parallel site-versus-wiki systems and new content types unless a concrete need is demonstrated. A page's authored Markus composition owns its editable content and supported embedded listings; reusable themes retain outer chrome, branding and presentation. Existing routes, content, canonical/SEO metadata, heading/link behavior and brand design must be preserved through migration. Exact path schema, composition/listing syntax and Markus-versus-Papyrus extension ownership remain unresolved design work; do not invent current directives or claim they already exist.

Shared behavior records: PPY-c08790af-4c51-4c9d-a7ae-7a3346504bb2 (one path-based page/content system), PPY-b6ede164-fad8-45da-a242-51362c5f8285 (authored homepage composition with reusable listings). Migration design task: PPY-d16f6481-3a24-4438-94cb-ac6ed8ef34e7. Help/wiki and ordinary site pages share this foundation and its construct-derived index/post-save refresh; neither wiki navigation nor product theming creates an independent content engine.

Final agreed authoring direction, planning only: “include” is the working construct name, not approved concrete syntax. It supports inclusion of a single page or a selected list. “Collection” means a selection of content, not a new storage object. On page/content save or compile, the supported pipeline scans/parses include constructs, updates the generated site-wide dependency index, and actually uses that index to regenerate affected pages; merely recording dependencies is incomplete. Reuse each include's rendering selection as the sole source of invalidation selection, with separate enforced publication/access/published gates. Nested/transitive includes, cycles, deduplication, edits/deletion and retries require observable behavior, not arbitrary-code inference.

RSS/Atom feed eligibility is distinct from page existence, include membership and navigation. An ordinary static wiki/help or product page does not automatically become a feed entry. Define shared feed selection/metadata and editorial eligibility without building a separate page or wiki engine. Exact include syntax, extension ownership and selection schema remain design questions; current Anth.us custom Python homepage code is evidence of a migration gap, not proof the proposed include construct is shipped.

Detailed include BDD: PPY-b6ede164-fad8-45da-a242-51362c5f8285. Author/operator documentation behavior: PPY-01b5e07f-773e-407f-9057-941f4e4c5a0c. Review must trace these scenarios through actual public output changes and failure recovery when implemented; documentation presence or an index write alone is insufficient.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Incorporated independent read-only architecture evidence at a1019e76: existing knowledgeQuery/vector retrieval and bounded graph/context packs are reuse candidates, not proof of safe public Help. Targeted validation task PPY-b14a72e4-0c44-4bb0-9b7f-92dae719f042 now blocks optional RAG Help and its cross-cutting review. Verify publication/tenant and access boundaries, published-only behavior, citations/freshness and actual per-publication index/graph population; approximate node/edge metadata is an audit lead, not a verified failure. No duplicated backend investigation or implementation.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Planning delivery: develop, Kanbus-only direct commit/push per repository policy; no PR required on the unprotected branch. Added 16 documentation/Help planning records (38 in the combined planning set). Verified all records through kbs show for exact descriptions, type/parent rules, Gherkin stories, open/unassigned state, agent provenance and dependency targets; full-board validation unchanged at 15 pre-existing abbreviated dependency errors. Workflow documentation stays under Monitoring (PPY-b6bc65, PPY-76a3bc), RSS (PPY-c4ea07) and headless (PPY-92de97); review tasks here are PPY-2ce2bc, PPY-7baa82, PPY-d943b5. RAG story PPY-14b972 and Help review PPY-d943b5 are blocked by PPY-b14a72 retrieval-boundary verification. Private Chattic.us-web source inspected read-only at 0f92209; existing migration work preserved. Independent backend findings are recorded as evidence requiring verification. All implementation unstarted; no repository creation, live changes, installs, deployment or model calls.
